summary: Static RLS defines fixed DAX filter rules per role in Power BI Desktop. Each role has one or more table filter expressions. Users assigned to a role see only rows matching those filters.
keyInsight: RLS is enforced in Power BI Service after publishing. RLS does NOT apply to workspace Admins, Members, or Contributors — they always see all data regardless of role assignments.
commonTrap: Thinking RLS applies to workspace members. Only users accessing data through Apps or as workspace Viewers have RLS enforced. Higher workspace roles bypass it entirely.

miniQuiz.question: A user is a Workspace Member and is also assigned to an RLS role filtered to the East region only. What data will they see?
choices: Only the East region — the RLS role restricts their view
All data — workspace Members bypass RLS
No data — RLS blocks all access for Members
Whichever is more restrictive — RLS or workspace role
miniQuiz.explanation: Workspace Admins, Members, and Contributors bypass RLS — they see all data regardless of role assignments. RLS only restricts Viewers or users accessing data through Apps.

summary: Dynamic RLS uses the current user's identity to filter data at runtime. The standard pattern matches [UserEmail] = USERPRINCIPALNAME() against a user-to-data mapping table.
keyInsight: Dynamic RLS requires a user-mapping table in the model. It scales to any number of users with a single role — adding a new user only requires adding a row to the mapping table.
commonTrap: Creating one static RLS role per user. With many users, static roles are unmanageable and require model republishing every time the user list changes.

miniQuiz.question: A company has 200 salespeople, each seeing only their own region's data. What is the most scalable RLS approach?
choices: Create 200 static RLS roles — one per salesperson
Create a user-mapping table and one dynamic RLS role using USERPRINCIPALNAME()
Create one role per region (10 regions = 10 roles)
Use sensitivity labels to restrict data access per user
miniQuiz.explanation: Dynamic RLS with a user-mapping table and USERPRINCIPALNAME() creates one role that automatically filters each user's data. New salespeople are added by inserting a row into the mapping table — no model changes needed.

summary: Power BI workspace roles in order of permission: Admin (full control), Member (publish, edit, manage access), Contributor (publish, edit), Viewer (read-only, RLS enforced).
keyInsight: Only the Viewer role enforces RLS. For broad, RLS-restricted read-only distribution to many users, publish an App — App audience members get Viewer-equivalent access with RLS applied.
commonTrap: Giving users Member or Contributor roles when they only need to view. These roles bypass RLS and expose all underlying data. Use Viewer or App distribution instead.

miniQuiz.question: You want 500 employees to view reports with RLS applied. What is the most appropriate distribution method?
choices: Add all 500 as Workspace Members
Add all 500 as Workspace Viewers
Publish an App and add the 500 employees as the App audience
Share individual reports with each employee
miniQuiz.explanation: Publishing an App and assigning users as the audience gives them viewer-level access with RLS enforced. It also provides a clean, managed distribution experience without exposing the workspace directly.

summary: Sensitivity labels (from Microsoft Purview) classify and protect Power BI content. Labels like Confidential or Highly Confidential can restrict sharing, export, and downstream use of data.
keyInsight: Sensitivity labels propagate downstream — when data is exported to Excel, the label follows it. This ensures protection outside of Power BI. Labels are configured in the Microsoft Purview compliance portal.
commonTrap: Thinking sensitivity labels enforce data access control (who can view). Labels classify and protect data after access — they do not restrict who can view a report. That is handled by workspace roles and RLS.

miniQuiz.question: An organization wants to prevent employees from exporting a dataset containing PII to unprotected Excel files. Which feature addresses this?
choices: Row-Level Security
Workspace Viewer role
Sensitivity labels with export restrictions
Disabled scheduled refresh
miniQuiz.explanation: Sensitivity labels can restrict export actions on classified content. A 'Highly Confidential' label prevents export to unprotected files or requires encryption when exported, protecting PII outside Power BI.

summary: An on-premises data gateway bridges Power BI Service to data sources inside an organizational network. Required for scheduled refresh of on-premises sources (SQL Server, Oracle, files, etc.).
keyInsight: Standard gateway supports multiple users and DirectQuery — required for enterprise use. Personal gateway is single-user only. Cloud sources (Azure SQL, SharePoint Online) do NOT need a gateway.
commonTrap: Assuming all data sources need a gateway. Gateways are only required for on-premises sources or sources within private VNets — not for cloud services.

miniQuiz.question: A scheduled refresh of a report connected to an on-premises SQL Server is failing. What is most likely missing?
choices: A Premium capacity license
An on-premises data gateway configured and running
A DirectQuery connection instead of Import
A certified dataset endorsement
miniQuiz.explanation: Scheduled refresh of on-premises SQL Server requires an on-premises data gateway to bridge the connection between Power BI Service (cloud) and the on-premises network. Without a gateway, refresh will always fail.

summary: Scheduled refresh automatically updates imported datasets on a defined schedule. Requires: dataset credentials configured, a gateway for on-premises sources, and a license within refresh frequency limits.
keyInsight: Pro license: up to 8 refreshes per day. Premium / Fabric: up to 48 refreshes per day. DirectQuery and DirectLake datasets do NOT use scheduled refresh — they query live data.
commonTrap: Expecting DirectQuery datasets to benefit from scheduled refresh. DirectQuery always queries the live source — there is no cached data to refresh.

miniQuiz.question: A Pro license user wants their Import mode dataset to refresh 10 times per day. What is the limitation?
choices: Pro license supports up to 8 refreshes per day — 10 requires Premium or Fabric capacity
Pro license supports unlimited scheduled refreshes
Import mode does not support scheduled refresh at all
Scheduled refresh requires a DirectQuery connection
miniQuiz.explanation: Power BI Pro limits scheduled refresh to 8 times per day. For 10+ daily refreshes, Premium Per User, Premium capacity, or Fabric is required — those support up to 48 refreshes per day.

summary: Endorsement labels mark datasets, reports, or dataflows as trustworthy. Promoted means the content owner vouches for it. Certified requires admin-level verification and carries the highest trust signal.
keyInsight: Certified content is the authoritative signal for organizational data assets. It appears prominently in dataset search and Lineage View, encouraging analysts to reuse governed datasets.
commonTrap: Confusing Promoted with Certified. Any dataset owner can Promote their content. Only authorized certifiers (configured by admins) can Certify — it is a formal governance checkpoint.

miniQuiz.question: A data team wants their master dataset to appear as the authoritative source for all reports across the company. Which endorsement level is most appropriate?
choices: Promoted — the owner can apply this themselves
Certified — requires admin verification and signals the highest organizational trust
Sensitivity label — Confidential
Featured — highlighted on the home experience
miniQuiz.explanation: Certified is the highest endorsement level. It signals organizational trust, appears in dataset search results and Lineage View, and encourages analysts to build on this authoritative, governed dataset.

summary: Deployment pipelines manage Power BI content lifecycle across Development, Test, and Production workspaces. Changes are promoted stage-by-stage with comparison views to see differences before deploying.
keyInsight: Deployment pipelines require Premium or Fabric capacity. They are the recommended ALM (Application Lifecycle Management) approach — ensuring changes are validated before reaching production users.
commonTrap: Manually copying PBIX files between workspaces as a deployment process. This is error-prone and does not preserve dataset configurations or data source settings. Deployment pipelines handle this automatically.

miniQuiz.question: An organization wants to test report changes in a staging environment before publishing to production. Which feature supports this workflow?
choices: Workspace roles with Contributor permissions for staging
Deployment pipelines with Development, Test, and Production stages
Scheduled refresh across multiple workspaces
Sensitivity labels with staged deployment rules
miniQuiz.explanation: Deployment pipelines provide a structured Dev → Test → Production promotion workflow with side-by-side comparison views, ensuring changes are validated before reaching production users.
